text:
Elias Lindholm came to Boston on a seven-year deal in 2024 to center the top line, and two quiet seasons later he's doing his best work from the third. He has 7 goals and 17 points in 20 games, his goals rank 20th of 530 skaters in wins added, and the Boston Globe had him with an NHL-leading 230 faceoff wins as of November 12.

Some of the scoring is borrowed. He's shooting 19.4% against a league norm of 13.3%, and his teammates have scored 4.41 more goals than expected with him on. His own chance rate, 0.91 expected goals per hour, is about where it was last season.

The part that looks real is the line's play. At five on five, Boston has had 58.4% of the expected goals with him on the ice, 5.93 points better than without him, a sharp turn from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting noticeably more with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged his signature pass: 23% of his setups go across the royal road, against 7% for a typical forward. Watch whether the defensive turnaround holds once the shooting cools.
headline: Elias Lindholm, third-line center, first-rate start
